snippet.title: Passion for Scent - The True Story of Perfume | Perfume Wasn't About Smelling Good
snippet.description:
Passion for Scent - The True Story of Perfume | Before perfume became luxury, it was obsession. This is the true story behind the world’s most iconic scent.

Director: Ina Knobloch
Genre: Documentary, History, Culture
Country: Germany
Language: English
Also Known As: The True Story of Perfume

Synopsis:
Passion for Scent – The True Story of Perfume explores the fascinating life of Giovanni Maria Farina, the creator of the legendary Eau de Cologne and one of the most influential perfume makers in history. The documentary traces his journey across Europe—from Italy to France and Germany—revealing how he mastered the art of fragrance and built a legacy that still endures today.

Along the way, the film draws intriguing parallels with Patrick Süskind’s Perfume: The Story of a Murderer, questioning whether fiction was inspired by real events. From royal courts to intellectual elites like Voltaire and Goethe, Farina’s creations captivated an entire era. The story also uncovers early cases of imitation and legal conflict, long before trademark laws existed. Ultimately, the documentary connects Farina’s legacy to the evolution of modern perfumery, including the rise of icons like Chanel No.5.

snippet.description:
Tiger Tanks: Hitler’s Most Feared Weapon and the Last Gamble of WWII explores the legend, power and limits of Germany’s most famous armored machines during the Second World War.

From Michael Wittmann’s famous Tiger tank action in Normandy to the desperate winter offensive in the Ardennes, this compilation follows the story of German armored warfare at its most feared and its most vulnerable. The Tiger, King Tiger, Jagdtiger, Panther and other late-war vehicles were powerful machines, but they also revealed the growing weaknesses of Nazi Germany: fuel shortages, mechanical breakdowns, impossible logistics and overwhelming Allied pressure.

The documentary examines the battlefield reputation of the Tiger tank, the propaganda value of Germany’s tank aces, the role of the Waffen-SS, and the brutal reality of the Battle of the Bulge, where Hitler committed his last major reserves in a failed attempt to split the Allied armies.

A mega documentary for viewers interested in World War II, German tanks, Tiger tanks, Michael Wittmann, the Battle of the Bulge, armored warfare and the final collapse of the Third Reich.

From Michael Wittmann’s famous Tiger tank action in Normandy to the desperate winter offensive in the Ardennes, this compilation follows the story of German armored warfare at its most feared and its most vulnerable. The Tiger, King Tiger, Jagdtiger, Panther and other late-war vehicles were powerful machines, but they also revealed the growing weaknesses of Nazi Germany: fuel shortages, mechanical breakdowns, impossible logistics and overwhelming Allied pressure.

The documentary examines the battlefield reputation of the Tiger tank, the propaganda value of Germany’s tank aces, the role of the Waffen-SS, and the brutal reality of the Battle of the Bulge, where Hitler committed his last major reserves in a failed attempt to split the Allied armies.

A mega documentary for viewers interested in World War II, German tanks, Tiger tanks, Michael Wittmann, the Battle of the Bulge, armored warfare and the final collapse of the Third Reich.

snippet.title: Who Killed Rollerblading? (Full Documentary)
snippet.description:
Who Killed Rollerblading? explores the meteoric rise and sudden fall of rollerblading in the 1990s and early 2000s. 

Through the story of its most iconic figure, Arlo Eisenberg, the film unravels how a once-exploding movement was cut down before it ever had the chance to fully take hold. From corporate backlash to its abrupt disappearance from the X Games, and a fervent rejection from skateboarders around the world (including VICE), a thriving subculture was pushed back into the shadows almost overnight. 

So we asked the question: who the hell killed rollerblading?
